impassioned

im-PASH-und -- three syllables, stress on the second syllable, PASH. · adjective

What It Means

Impassioned is showing or filled with great emotion.

The coach's impassioned halftime talk turned the whole game around.

Worked Example

At the town meeting, a neighbor rises to defend the ancient oak on Elm Street. Halfway through, she abandons her notecards entirely -- her voice cracks, her hands fly, and when she finally sits down, the room is silent.

Her speech was impassioned: filled with great emotion on full display. Impassioned describes the delivery -- the plea, the appeal, the speech -- at one charged moment. It is about how the feeling pours out, not about a person's lasting temperament.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

fiery: Fiery describes a speaker's whole style -- a fiery senator blazes in every debate, on every topic, every week. Impassioned belongs to one charged moment: a single plea, speech, or letter filled with great emotion, even from someone otherwise quiet.

stirring: Stirring describes the effect on the audience -- a stirring anthem rouses strong emotion in the people listening. Impassioned describes the speaker's side: the deep feeling pouring out of the person delivering the words, whether or not anyone listening is moved.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

halfhearted: done with little energy or enthusiasm

unemotional: showing no feeling at all

Where it sits · how deep the feeling behind it runs — heated → impassioned → overwrought

heated vs. impassioned: Heated only says the temperature rose -- a heated exchange can be nothing but temper -- while an impassioned speech burns with deep feeling for a cause, not just irritation.

overwrought vs. impassioned: Overwrought goes further than impassioned: an impassioned speaker is filled with deep feeling but still in command of it, while an overwrought one has been overwhelmed -- the emotion runs the speaker instead of the speech.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — im-

prefix — im-: in, into (Latin in-)

root — passion-

root — passion-: strong feeling; suffering (Latin passio, from pati 'to feel, to suffer')

suffix — -ed

suffix — -ed: having, filled with (Old English)

Put it together

Put it together: Impassioned is literally 'filled with passion' -- im- ('in') puts the passion into the speaker, and -ed marks the state of being full of it. An impassioned plea is one into which deep feeling has been poured until it overflows.

Use the root in a new word: compassionate

Use the root in a new word: compassionate: The compassionate nurse sat with the frightened boy until his parents arrived.

Root Check

Word Choice

Impassioned attaches to moments of expression: an impassioned plea, speech, defense, letter. It describes how feeling comes out at one charged moment. Its cluster neighbor fervent describes the feeling itself, which may stay quietly inside -- a fervent believer might never give an impassioned speech in her life.
